450	Not that we are anything on our own, HaShem
451	channels abundance to the world through us, but a person can stop
452	and say: wow, how much good, how much good I have now.
453	Not in the sense of — we have to be careful here — not in the sense
454	of pride, or that I have nothing to correct, heaven forbid.
455	Not in that place. But truly, truly walking
456	through the world saying: wow, how much good. To recognize
457	the good. Do you recognize your own good at all, or are you
458	busy all day with, you know, eating yourself up
459	inside? Do you live with an inner stance of: wow,
460	I recognize the good?
461	Recognizing the good. And to recognize the good, or the
462	depth of the good of a Jew, is to understand that you are a part
463	of God above. Truly. What they feared, what the people
464	feared, according to some explanations, the complainers. How does
465	Rashi put it? That they sought a pretext to withdraw from the Place.
466	Suddenly they begin to understand that the whole understanding of recognizing
467	the good in me, recognizing the good in me, looking at how much good
468	there is in me, how much good — in its depth, it leads me
469	to — do you know what this good that you have is? First, who
470	gave it to you? Clearly it is HaShem. And it is
471	clear that you are a Divine revelation, a chariot for the Shechinah.
472	As if HaShem, whose glory fills the whole earth,
473	chose that you would live. He wants you. He gives you life,
474	brings you into being, gives, lights you up in the morning, because He
475	wants you. That is the depth of the good. And this depth of the good
476	cannot be separate from HaShem, who
477	is the One who gives us life. He is all of life, He is everything. He is
478	everything, the Creator of the world.
479	And so a Jew walking through the world like this is, in fact, as
480	the Netivot Shalom says, the correction. If
481	sin is the distance, it is understanding that the graver
482	the sin, the more it separates me from devekut
483	and from love of HaShem, then we understand
484	that the correction is the opposite. It is whatever connects me most
485	to HaShem, whatever connects me most to devekut
486	with Him. How do I go about fulfilling the
487	mitzvot, not as a rote commandment of men, though that too is
488	important to do, because it is the will of HaShem, but I
489	go with an inner demand to love, to cleave,
490	to be as attached as possible to HaShem, to want
491	this most, to rejoice in it most. And this comes, the Rav says,
492	through the mightiest emotion among all the emotions
493	of human uprightness: that a person recognizes the good. Recognizes the
494	good, and the more I recognize the good, the happier I am
495	to cleave to HaShem. I want it.
496	I seek HaShem — not "demand," I
497	want to bring joy. Someone did me good, I want
498	only to help him somehow, for him to tell me how I
499	can help him, how I can do him good. And this is
500	in fact the secret of the correction that the people of Israel perhaps went through
501	during the forty years that followed the sin of
502	the complainers. There are explanations for the forty years, all kinds
503	of explanations why forty years; the sin of the spies is
504	the main one, but there are also commentators who say it was the sin of
505	the complainers, that there is something here that, wow,
506	takes forty years to set right. What is
507	this? How did you see everything you
508	saw? What, are you out of your minds?
509	Now, this is not a statement about them, heaven forbid. We
510	are not speaking about the people of Israel as some category. It is
511	a statement about us: how do you look at your life?
512	If someone could look at you from the outside, he would say to you: are you
513	normal? Look how much good you have, how much light you have,
514	how much light you have and how much light is within you.
515	And what do you do? How do you
516	spend all day in a stance of complaining, all day
517	complaining, all day "I am not enough for you"?
518	How do you turn the picture around? Through recognizing the good,
519	the mightiest emotion, the mightiest among all the emotions
520	of human uprightness. Come on, may we merit, with the help of HaShem,
521	to be full of our good, full of the Divine light
522	that is revealed within us, and to shine it into the world. May it be
523	for you entirely only good.
